david-whittaker.name: David Whittaker
david-whittaker.bio: David Whittaker is an English video-game composer and programmer whose work spans many of the major home-computer formats of the 1980s and early 1990s. He wrote a very large catalogue of game music, including Lazy Jones and numerous C64 and Amiga scores, and later moved into audio and dialogue work for companies including Electronic Arts and Traveller's Tales.

ed-bogas.name: Ed Bogas
ed-bogas.bio: Ed Bogas is an American composer whose career spans records, film, television and video games. Alongside screen work including animation, he contributed music to a number of 1980s computer games; the CCG archive links him to Card Sharks, Law of the West, Murder on the Mississippi and Park Patrol.

francis-mechner.name: Francis Mechner
francis-mechner.bio: Francis Mechner is a psychologist, educator and accomplished pianist who also composed music for games created by his son Jordan Mechner. His game credits include Karateka and Prince of Persia, giving his musical work a small but distinctive place in early computer-game history.

franck-sauer.name: Franck Sauer
franck-sauer.bio: Franck Sauer is a Belgian game artist, designer and composer whose career began on the Commodore 64 before moving to major Amiga projects. He worked at Ubisoft, helped create Unreal and Agony, later co-founded Art & Magic, and continued in senior art roles including work on Outcast.

frank-klepacki.name: Frank Klepacki
frank-klepacki.bio: Frank Klepacki is an American composer, musician and sound designer best known for his long association with Westwood Studios and the Command & Conquer series. His earlier game work includes Dune II and Eye of the Beholder II, both represented in the CCG Amiga archive, and he later continued composing through Petroglyph and independent projects.

fred-gray.name: Fred Gray
fred-gray.bio: Fred Gray is an English game composer closely associated with Commodore 64 music of the mid-to-late 1980s. His credits include Shadowfire, Mutants, Nodes of Yesod, Frankie Goes to Hollywood and many other titles, with work for companies including Imagine, Ocean and Odin. Published sources conflict on his birth year, so it is intentionally omitted.

gary-biasillo.name: Gary Biasillo
gary-biasillo.bio: Gari Biasillo is a British programmer and musician who entered the games industry straight from school, working first at Interceptor and later on multi-platform projects including work connected with Ocean. His C64 credits in the CCG archive include Joe Blade and Target Renegade.

george-neophytou.name: George Neophytou
george-neophytou.bio: George Neophytou is a British C64-era music contributor whose preserved credits include Jet Set Willy and The Faces of Haarne. Public biographical information is limited, so the CCG profile concentrates on documented game-audio credits rather than unsupported personal details.

sources.title: MobyGames and preserved C64 credit records

graham-jarvis.name: Graham Jarvis
graham-jarvis.bio: Graham Jarvis is a British media composer whose game work included a partnership with Rob Hartshorne through Clever Music. He contributed to a range of C64 projects before moving further into television and production music, with CCG-linked credits including Back to the Future, Blade Runner, The Rocky Horror Show and Shao-Lin's Road.

graham-marsh.name: Graham Marsh
graham-marsh.bio: Graham Marsh is an English electronics engineer and C64 musician known in the scene as Mighty Bogg. In interviews he has described growing up in Wakefield and combining electronics, programming and music; his CCG credits include Dan Dare: Pilot of the Future and Spiky Harold.

gregory-haggard.name: Gregory Haggard
gregory-haggard.bio: Gregory Haggard is an American composer and music educator whose professional background includes screen and game music as well as later academic work. The CCG archive links him to Cinemaware's It Came from the Desert, Antheads and Wings on the Amiga.

james-lisney.name: James Lisney
james-lisney.bio: James Lisney is an English concert pianist whose career is primarily in classical performance. During the early Commodore 64 era he also arranged music for Jeff Minter's games, including Hover Bovver, Revenge of the Mutant Camels and Sheep in Space.
